rv.q: All together, Venus proves itself to be a thrilling start to Woolly Mammoth’s new season.
There’s nothing not to like about “Venus.”
What stayed with me most was how funny the production remains even as it becomes increasingly disturbing.
Aesthetically, he outfits Yockey’s play with a stylish, speculative bent that makes the big realization rewarding.
This huge, never-explained sculpture is our first clue that the old, weird Woolly is back .
Set in a universe that veers between the magical and the terrifying, Venus leaves the audience exhilarated.

In Venus , the company's season-opening world premiere directed by White, that ethos that has come to define this company has made a triumphant return via his smart directorial touch and two performances that are at the same time funny, perplexing, and simply crazy.

cn.t: Steve Yockey's darkly comic "Venus" earns praise as a wildly entertaining, thrilling exploration of modern romance gone hilariously and horrifyingly wrong, elevated by excellent performances and Woolly Mammoth's signature weird, provocative style.
